This makes the bug WEAKER than the other clean default-path released-to-released DeepXDE positives (Neumann, periodic_point, resample, boundary_float32) and is recorded as such. It is nonetheless a genuine, upstream-fixed operator self-adjointness defect with zero confounders, reproduced via the EXACT buggy code object (byte-identical to the repo source at the commit).

upstream: DeepXDE git commit 46e2c2e (#1591, author Zongren Zou). Root cause in deepxde/gradients/gradients_forward.py: the forward-mode Jacobian cache self.J is keyed by the INPUT-axis index j (it stores dy/dx_j computed via jax.jvp along basis tangent e_j). The dim_y==1 branch returned self.J[i] (indexed by OUTPUT row i, always 0 for a scalar field), so every requested column k returned column 0; off-diagonal Hessian entries built by composing two forward Jacobians become wrong and ASYMMETRIC. The fix returns self.J[j] (input column). The same commit also defaults hessian(component=None) -> 0 (PRE raised TypeError because the inner jacobian(i=None) hit `0 <= i`).
